Under the stated assumption, the Weisfeiler-Lehman (WL) injectivity condition for updating a vertex feature at iteration k can be written as an injective multiset-to-label mapping:

h_v^{(k)} = \phi\Big(h_v^{(k-1)},\; \multiset{h_u^{(k-1)} : u \in N(v)}\Big),

with the injectivity requirement

\phi(a, M) = \phi(b, N) \iff a=b \text{ and } M=N,

where h_v^{(k)} is the feature/label of vertex v after k WL iterations, N(v) is the neighborhood of v, and \phi is an injective hash or update function. In the GIN formulation, this is commonly implemented as

h_v^{(k)} = \mathrm{MLP}^{(k)}\Big((1+\epsilon^{(k)})h_v^{(k-1)} + \sum_{u\in N(v)} h_u^{(k-1)}\Big),

which is designed to be as expressive as the WL test when the MLP is injective over the aggregated neighborhood representation. Note that original DeepWalk does not use GIN or WL hashing; this equation is the WL-style injective update rule you asked for under the hypothetical assumption.
